status_detail: Kosciusko County Commissioners voted 3-0 on April 22, 2025 to deny rezoning of more than 500 acres from agricultural to industrial use after the Area Plan Commission recommended denial 8-0.
notes: Proposed site was roughly 550-554 acres near Leesburg/CR 700N and CR 300W by NIPSCO transmission infrastructure. News reports state Prologis would not pursue another Kosciusko County location after denial.

status_detail: No specific data center project found in official county/plan commission/EDA searches; only regulatory moratorium activity located.
notes: Local reporting says the Plan Commission recommended and county officials moved toward/approved a data center moratorium to study impacts; no named developer, site, permit, rezoning case, or project application was found.

project_name: Microsoft La Porte data center campus
status_detail: City/state announcement identified a $1 billion, 245,000-square-foot data center on 489 acres at Radius Industrial Park; Microsoft local updates and subsequent reporting indicate site preparation/groundbreaking in 2026.
notes: Official city release says construction/operations timeline depended on design, planning and permitting; Microsoft later said it is building in La Porte. MW not found in official source.

status_detail: Michigan City major-project page says Phoenix Investors and its end-user propose redeveloping the vacant former Federal-Mogul facility at 402 Royal Road into a modern data center campus and lists building permits, IDEM records, zoning verification, tax abatement, and taxpayer agreement documents.
notes: Official city page describes 380,000-400,000 square feet of reuse, customer-owned substation, utility upgrades, mechanical/electrical yards, and possible expansion areas. DCD reports Project Maize is in LaPorte County with $832 million investment by 2034.

aliases: Sentinel Data Centers Eagle Creek Township data center
status_detail: Project information site describes a proposed data center in unincorporated Lake County. Local reporting says Lake County Council approved the rezoning 6-0 on June 9, 2026; later special exception and site plan approvals are still required before building permits.
notes: Reported as roughly 160 acres in Eagle Creek Township, south side of Indiana 2/east of Clay Street, with approximately $5 billion investment and 500 MW. Project site says rezoning alone does not authorize construction.

status_detail: No specific Lawrence County, Indiana data center project found after checking county official site, Economic Growth Council pages, and web/news searches.
notes: Search results for Lawrence County data centers largely referred either to generic service-provider pages or Lawrence County, Ohio. The LCEGC 'Data Center' page is demographic/commuting data, not a data center facility project.

status_detail: No named Madison County, Indiana data center project found; county is in moratorium/regulatory review posture.
notes: Indiana Public Radio reported commissioners adopted a pause in June 2026 and extended it to a full year on August 4, 2026 while drafting zoning rules; no project sponsor, parcel, permit, or rezoning case was identified.

project_name: Sabey Decatur Technology Park data center
status_detail: Metropolitan Development Commission approved the $4 billion, 130-acre Decatur Township data center on March 18, 2026. Developer materials show two buildings and utility ramp to 250 MW over five years.
notes: Developer site describes Building A at about 572,500 sf, Building B at about 490,000 sf, a 10-acre substation, phased permitting/site prep beginning 2026, and AES infrastructure upgrades by Q4 2027.

status_detail: Metrobloks developer page lists IND A1 at 2505 N Sherman Dr as coming soon with 72 MW total critical IT and 154K sf whitespace. Local reporting says the Metropolitan Development Commission approved the nearly 14-acre, $500 million project 6-2 on April 1, 2026.
notes: Site is the former Sherman Drive-In Theater near 25th Street and Sherman Drive in Martindale Brightwood. News reported final council handling could still occur, but later moratorium reporting treats Metrobloks as already approved/exempt.

status_detail: DC BLOX project page describes two data center buildings across two phases at Thunderbird Commerce Center with $1.8-$2.0 billion investment. Mirror Indy reported MDC approved the project 6-1 on July 15, 2026 and no further approvals were needed, though judicial review was possible.
notes: Brownfield redevelopment at former Ford/Visteon Thunderbird Commerce Center near South Kitley Avenue/Pennsy Trail in Warren Township/Irvington area. Scaled-back plan reported as two-building campus with 31 diesel generators, 600 construction jobs and 21 permanent jobs.

project_name: American Tower Pike Township data center proposal
status_detail: Developer withdrew plans for a 20,000-square-foot unmanned data center in Pike Township amid neighborhood opposition; tracker lists the project as canceled.
notes: Reported site was near W. 79th Street and Township Line Road; Cleanview lists 53 acres, 20,000 sf, 4 MW, status canceled. Treating withdrawn/canceled proposal as rejected for allowed status vocabulary.

status_detail: Lifeline states it purchased the 41-acre former Eastgate mall in 2008 and opened the first data center building in 2009; current official pages list Eastgate at 401 N Shadeland Ave as an Indiana data center location.
notes: Official Lifeline page lists 80,000 square feet at 401 N Shadeland Ave; Baxtel market page identifies Lifeline Eastgate as Indianapolis' largest data center at 9 MW and 80,000 sf.

project_name: Netrality Indy Telcom Center / 733 West Henry
status_detail: Netrality official facility page identifies 733 West Henry as an operational Indianapolis core interconnection/colocation data center on the Indy Telcom campus; Netrality announced acquisition of Lifeline's 733 West Henry facility in 2022.
notes: Facility page lists carrier-neutral MMR, 36+ on-net network providers, 24/7 NOC, and retail colocation configurations. Capacity not found in official source.

status_detail: No specific project found; Marshall County enacted a countywide prohibition on data centers after earlier moratorium discussions.
notes: Official plan commission document describes a request to update the zoning ordinance to prohibit data centers. News reports say commissioners approved the permanent ban on April 20, 2026, effective immediately.
